name: Mississippi
about: The blueprint of Mississippi (perfectnations.com/perfect-states/mississippi/). Census, NAEP and USDA figures marked "computed" are read by tools/build_us_state.py from data/us/raw/mississippi/ and data/us-states.json. No figure is estimated.
notes: v1.0: Perfect Mississippi, a Perfect States blueprint (Preeti Sinha, President and CEO, 25 Nov 2026: "go ahead and implement" the Perfect States plan). Water and Energy are shown as not yet measured: no primary state figure was confirmed.

hero.line: A computed:gdp_words economy where computed:poverty of Mississippians live below the poverty line, and fourth graders now read above the national average.
hero.sub: Perfect Nations counts what Mississippi owns, prices the seven basic standards of living for every resident, and designs the capital that closes the gap.

assets.title: Five assets that can carry Perfect Mississippi.
assets.line: Each is owned by Mississippians today and can carry a standard of living.

items.name: The pension fund
items.line: The Public Employees’ Retirement System of Mississippi, invested for teachers, state and local workers.

items.name: The forests
items.line: Forest covers 64% of the State’s land, a renewable source of timber and carbon value.

items.name: The school trust land
items.line: Sixteenth Section lands held in trust for public schools and leased by 101 school districts.

items.name: The rainy day fund
items.line: The Working Cash Stabilization Reserve Fund, unallocated in the fiscal 2027 budget recommendation.

items.name: The people
items.line: Mississippians on 1 July 2025: the asset every other asset serves.

solutions.title: Solutions for Perfect Mississippi, in order.
solutions.line: Livelihood first: the reading reform shows what Mississippi can do; incomes come next.

items.challenge: computed:poverty of Mississippians lived below the poverty line in 2025; 36.4% in Holmes County (2020–2024).
items.advises: Turn the forests and school trust land into income: a Delta enterprise fund that invests in timber, processing and jobs in the poorest counties, with returns shared with the school trust.

items.challenge: computed:food of households were food insecure in 2022–2024, above the national computed:food_us.
items.advises: Put the savings from SNAP accuracy (band 05) into a food fund with Mississippi food banks and grocers, starting in the Delta.

items.challenge: computed:uninsured of Mississippians had no health insurance in 2025.
items.advises: Pay rural clinics on outcomes through a health-access bond, repaid from savings in uncompensated hospital care.

solutions.hold: Phase 3, hold the line: reading (computed:reading at the NAEP Proficient level, above the nation) and shelter (1,245 without a home on one night, January 2025), with water and energy measured next.

capital.title: Mississippi already finances its recovery.
capital.line: Instruments on record that a Perfect Mississippi can build on.

items.name: The BP economic settlement
items.line: Paid to the State from 2016 to 2033 for economic damage from the 2010 oil spill.

items.name: The Gulf Coast Restoration Fund
items.line: A year for growth in the six southernmost counties, from the BP settlement.

items.name: The Capital Expense Fund
items.line: Unallocated in the fiscal 2027 budget recommendation, for one-time investment.

items.name: Gulf Environmental Benefit Fund
items.line: For natural resource projects on the Mississippi coast, from the BP and Transocean plea agreements.

intelligence.title: A $75m SNAP bill that accuracy can cut.
intelligence.line: From October 2027 every state pays part of its SNAP food benefits unless at least 94 of every 100 dollars are paid exactly right. AI that checks every case before it is paid can shrink that bill.
intelligence.bill_label: a year in SNAP benefits from October 2027, at the 2025 error rate

facts.label: of SNAP dollars paid in error, 2025
share of benefits the State pays from October 2027

intelligence.advises: Bring the error rate under 8% and the share halves to 5%, about $37m a year saved. Build AI checks into the State’s new eligibility system, and audit them every quarter for underpayments as well as overpayments.
